name: Tempester n°37: dead code of the official OS erased (9,876 bytes freed)
explanation: Room for new features: 38 runs of the official code that nothing can execute any more on 1.6.3.0 are filled with 0xFF (erased flash), 9,876 bytes in total, each run at least 64 bytes. Every run is dead with the verdict « proven » of tools/reachability.py on the 1.6.3.0 image: not reached from the reset entry, the vectors or any code pointer (aligned and unaligned pointer words anywhere in the image, lui/addiu and lui/ori pairs, jump tables), no pointer from a live source into it, no live immediate built on its address; Ghidra's own references of the same image land on the same live code (tools/reachability_ghidra_check.py). « Probable » ranges (the case blocks of a dead dispatcher, kept only by its dead jump table), nop padding, runs under 64 bytes, words already written by another patch, rodata, the crt0, the vectors and the flasher page are not touched. What is erased: the C library's unused text formatter (2,228 bytes), unused soft-float and 64-bit helpers of the compiler library (1,648 bytes), file-system API calls nothing calls (1,852 bytes), a USB buffer-descriptor helper, a NOR flash chip-erase routine, MIDI DIN send helpers and MIDI status-length helpers, a Panel bus byte writer, Play List and beat helpers without caller, two delay loops, and three pieces made dead by Tempester patches: the two copies of the LFO Restart = Play loop in the Timer 1 interrupt (n°17 runs it from Timer 4) and the old DIN NRPN/RPN parser (n°9a parses NRPN on both inputs). Hence n°37 requires n°9a and n°17, and a later patch that calls one of these routines again must first take its run out of this recipe. Checked: the patched image reaches exactly the same instructions as 1.6.3.0, no filled word is reached or pointed to (tools/dead_code_reclaim.py check, with counter-proofs: a live routine, a probable range or a pointer-only routine erased is refused), and every firmware simulation of 1.6.3.0 passes on it. The Main OS dump read back from the machine shows 0xFF in these runs. Docs/analyses/opt-dead-code.md §13 lists the freed runs.
